title: Trellis K8 Vision Tower Round-Trip Error
method: EXL3 trellis K8 round-trip on all 111 2D vision weight tensors (27 ViT blocks × 4 weights + merger × 2 + pos_embed). quantize_exl3 (uncalibrated, meta Hessian) + ext.reconstruct + hadamard_fold_weight. MLP weights with dim 4304 (not 128-aligned) padded to 4352 before encoding, cropped back after. KLD suite is text-only (no images), so vision weights don't affect KLD — this measures round-trip error on the weights themselves.
vision_tower: Qwen3.8 ViT: 27 blocks, hidden=1152, MLP=4304, merger=[4608→5120]

blocks.N.mlp.linear_fc1.weight.note: K=4304 not 128-aligned, padded to 4352 (34×128) for Hadamard fold, cropped back

blocks.N.mlp.linear_fc2.weight.note: N=4304 not 128-aligned, padded to 4352 (34×128) for Hadamard fold, cropped back

model.visual.pos_embed.weight.note: Higher MSE due to small tensor with large dynamic range; max_err=0.111 but cosine still >1.0

key_findings: Trellis K8 round-trip on vision tower is near-lossless: overall proxy error 0.000020, MSE 1.06e-08, cosine 0.99998.
Proxy error (0.000020) matches the embedding K8 proxy error (0.000019) — trellis K8 coding is consistent across tensor types.
Padding approach for 4304-dim MLP weights works: proxy errors (0.000019-0.000020) are indistinguishable from non-padded weights.
All 111 tensors (458.5M params, 0.917 GB BF16) compress to 0.459 GB at K8 — saving 0.459 GB (50% reduction).
pos_embed has highest MSE (3.93e-07) and max_err (0.111) — small tensor with large values, but cosine still >1.0.
Vision tower does NOT affect the text-only KLD suite (no images in the 512 contexts), so KLD is unchanged from the baseline.
Combined with trellis K8 embeddings (0.002653 mean KLD), the total quantization footprint would be: embeddings K8 + vision K8, with no additional KLD impact beyond the embedding quantization.

comparison_with_embedding_k8.note: Embedding K8 saves ~1.27 GB, vision K8 saves ~0.46 GB, total ~1.50 GB from BF16→K8 trellis.
